summary:
Finger-sized minis, Mi and Ni, live on the Moon. One day they hear a song playing from a cassette left behind at the Apollo 11 site, and they fall in love with it. Searching through everything else the Apollo missions abandoned, they discover that the music comes from Earth. Among the objects they find a sketch of a spaceship: the way to go and get more music.

MINIS DON’T DISCARD is a free, 3D, online MULTIPLAYER game where friends join as Mi or Ni, explore the Apollo landing sites and build that ship together, piece by piece, as the first step toward Earth.

Our challenge is pedagogy: a list of discarded equipment is easy to forget, but a story you live with friends is not. Every artifact the players find opens a notebook page with a real NASA photo, a short story and a link to its source. Text is bilingual (English/Spanish), so kids from many countries can learn the same history.

The game turns “abandoned but not forgotten” into an adventure: nothing on the Moon is trash, and every object has a story. It runs in any browser, with no install and no account.
details:
The story. Mi and Ni are two finger-sized minis who live on the Moon. At the Apollo 11 site they hear a song coming from a cassette the astronauts left behind, and they fall in love with it. They search through everything else the Apollo missions abandoned and discover that the music comes from Earth. Among the objects they find a sketch of a spaceship: the way to go and get more music.

What it does. MINIS DON’T DISCARD is a free, 3D, online MULTIPLAYER game. Players choose Mi or Ni and play alone or create a room and share a code with friends. After a short cinematic, they explore the Apollo sites, carry (E) and drop real artifacts, and look (Q) at them to open a notebook page with a NASA photo, a short story and the link to its source. The ship is built by the team, piece by piece, so cooperation is part of the game.

Why it works (pedagogy). Our challenge is to bring NASA’s lunar heritage to children and teenagers. A list of discarded equipment is easy to forget, but a story you live with friends is not. We combine two approaches that education research supports: digital storytelling, cooperative learning and computer-supported collaborative learning. Text is bilingual (English/Spanish), so kids from many countries can learn the same history.

Intended impact. Players learn that nothing on the Moon is trash and every object has a story: “abandoned but not forgotten” becomes an adventure they remember and share.

How we built it. JavaScript and Three.js (3D world, toon-shaded characters, animations), a Node.js server for multiplayer rooms, and a notebook-style interface. It runs in any browser, with no install and no account.
